mainTopic: Cases where one offering covers many events: the נזיר, the סוטה, the מצורע and the woman with several births.
overview: This amud finishes the list of cases where one offering covers many events. First, a פסוק teaches that a separate offering is needed for each different שפחה חרופה. Next, רב חסדא proves that the משנה's rule for a נזיר impure many times follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who holds that the new נזירות begins on the seventh day, and not רבי, who holds it begins on the eighth. The next משנה adds a husband who warned his wife about many men and a מצורע afflicted many times. Each has a 'זאת תורת' פסוק teaching one offering for many. The משנה's line about birds brought before a new affliction seems to require extra offerings. The גמרא fixes it to be about when the מצורע's poor or rich status is set, and brings a three-way dispute that all comes from the word 'בטהרתו'. The last משנה covers a woman with several births or miscarriages. The גמרא gives its source and rewords a ברייתא about what 'זאת' excludes. It then shows that רבי יהודה counts from the first fetus even with twins. The amud ends as a new question is introduced, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A separate offering for each maidservant
steps.stepSummary: The words 'and she is a maidservant' teach that someone who sins with several different שפחות חרופות brings a separate offering for each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words "and she is a maidservant" come to separate: a separate offering for each and every maidservant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier derivation. It reads the words 'and she is a maidservant' as a source that each different שפחה requires her own offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that repeated sins with one שפחה חרופה need only one אשם. But when there are several different women, the פסוק teaches לחלק, to split them up. Each woman is a separate sin with its own offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Maidservant. Here it means a שפחה חרופה, a maidservant who is designated to a man.
To separate. The פסוק comes to make each case count on its own.
Each and every maidservant, counted one by one.

steps.whatToRemember: With several different שפחות חרופות, each one requires her own offering, and the source is the words 'and she is a maidservant'.

phrases.english: "And she is a maidservant"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:20

phrases.english: comes to separate, for each and every maidservant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a derivation that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each separate שפחה חרופה requires her own offering.

steps.title: Who taught the rule about the impure nazirite?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a נזיר who became impure many times and asks which תנא holds that he brings only one קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A נזיר who became impure many times brings one קרבן. Who is the תנא who taught this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new case in the משנה and asks whose opinion it follows. This sets up רב חסדא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that a נזיר who became impure many times brings only one קרבן. The גמרא wants to know which opinion makes this case possible, because it depends on when a נזיר's new period of נזירות begins after he becomes pure again.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who took a vow to avoid wine, haircuts and impurity from the dead.
Many separate times of becoming impure.
Who is the תנא? This asks whose opinion the משנה follows.

phrases.english: A nazirite who became impure with many impurities.
Who is the tanna who taught this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the שפחה case to the next case in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view allows a case where a נזיר has many impurities and still brings only one קרבן.

steps.title: רב חסדא: It is רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the משנה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who holds that the new pure נזירות begins on the seventh day. So a נזיר who becomes impure on the seventh day, and again on a later seventh day, brings only one קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who says that the pure נזירות takes effect from the seventh day. You can find this case when he became impure on the seventh day, and then again became impure on the seventh day. Since the proper time to bring the קרבן never came, he must bring only one קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. He names the תנא and describes the exact case that fits the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An impure נזיר counts seven days of purification and brings his קרבנות on the eighth day. According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, his new pure נזירות already begins on the seventh day, so becoming impure on the seventh day counts as a new impurity. But the eighth day never arrived, so all these impurities together need only one קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The new pure period of נזירות that the נזיר starts again after becoming pure.
Takes effect, begins to apply.
You can find it, meaning this is a real case where the rule applies.
The time that is fit for bringing the קרבן, which is the eighth day.

steps.confusionAlert: The question here is not whether he is impure. The question is when the new pure נזירות begins, the seventh day or the eighth day. That decides whether the second impurity counts as a new one.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda,
who says: the naziriteship of purity
takes effect on him from the seventh day.
phrases.notes: The seventh day of his purification, the day he immerses.

phrases.english: And you find it, for example, where he became impure on the seventh,
and again became impure on the seventh,
phrases.notes: He counted seven new days and became impure again on that new seventh day.

phrases.english: and since the time had not come
that is fit for bringing a קרבן on it,
phrases.notes: He means the eighth day, which he never reached.

phrases.english: he is liable to bring only one קרבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מאן תנא question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. In his view the new נזירות starts on the seventh day, so repeated impurity on seventh days is a real case of several impurities, and it requires one קרבן because the eighth day never came.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the משנה's case depends on the argument over when the נזיר's new pure נזירות begins.

steps.title: Why the משנה cannot follow רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that according to רבי, the new נזירות does not begin until the eighth day. So impurity on the seventh day is just one long continuous impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if it follows רבי: since רבי says the pure נזירות does not take effect on him until the eighth day, then if he became impure on the seventh and again became impure on the seventh, it is all one long impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא is explaining why he did not say the משנה follows רבי. He covers the seventh-day case here, and the next step covers the eighth-day case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, the new pure נזירות starts only on the eighth day, after the קרבנות. So becoming impure again on the seventh day does not break any new נזירות. It simply continues the first impurity, so it is not really a case of 'many impurities' at all.

keyTerms.meaning: For if, which introduces the reason for rejecting the other option.
The eighth day, when the נזיר brings his קרבנות.
One long, stretched-out impurity, not separate impurities.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: the new נזירות starts on the seventh day. רבי: it starts only on the eighth day. Under רבי, impurity on the seventh day is just one long impurity.

phrases.english: For if it is Rebbi,
phrases.notes: רבי means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: since Rebbi says:
the naziriteship of purity, until the eighth day,
does not take effect on him,
if he became impure on the seventh
and again became impure on the seventh,
it is all one long impurity,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's answer by showing that the other main view does not fit the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Under רבי, impurity on the seventh day is not a new impurity but part of one long impurity, so the case in step 3 does not work for him.

steps.title: Under רבי, impurity on the eighth day would require a separate offering each time
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא shows that under רבי the eighth-day case cannot fit the משנה either, because once the time for the offering has arrived, each new impurity requires its own קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the case is where he became impure on the eighth day, and then again on a later eighth day: since the proper time to bring an offering had already arrived, he is obligated in a separate offering for each one!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא checks the other possible case under רבי, impurity on the eighth day, and shows that it gives the wrong result for the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי, impurity on the seventh day is just one continuous impurity, so the משנה's 'many times' does not fit. Impurity on the eighth day also does not fit, because by then he was fit to bring his קרבן, and each new impurity counts on its own. So no case under רבי gives 'many impurities with only one קרבן'.

keyTerms.meaning: The eighth day of the נזיר's purification, when he brings his offerings
The moment has arrived (literally, 'the hour went out')
Fit to bring an offering
He is liable for each and every one separately

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question against רבי himself. רב חסדא is using רבי's view to show that the משנה cannot be following רבי.

phrases.english: If he became impure on the eighth day
and then became impure again on a later eighth day,
since the time had arrived
when it was fit to bring an offering,
he is obligated for each and every one!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּנִטְמָא בַּשְּׁמִינִי וְחָזַר וְנִטְמָא בַּשְּׁמִינִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the second half of the argument about רבי: the seventh-day case does not work (Step 4), and the eighth-day case does not work either.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that the משנה follows רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On the eighth day the time for the קרבן has arrived, so each impurity requires its own offering. That contradicts the משנה's ruling of only one קרבן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Under רבי, impurity on the eighth day comes after the time for the קרבן has arrived, so each impurity needs its own offering. That also fails to fit the משנה.

steps.title: So the משנה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Since neither case works under רבי, רב חסדא concludes that the משנה must follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: the משנה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא closes his proof: the only view that fits the משנה is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the new נזירות starts on the seventh day, so impurity on the seventh day is a real new impurity. But the time for the קרבן (the eighth day) has not yet come, so many such impurities share one קרבן. That is exactly the משנה's case.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces the conclusion after other options are ruled out
Learn from this; a firm conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: The נזיר case of 'one קרבן for many impurities' works only under רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: impurity on the seventh day counts as new, but the offering time has not yet come.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this
that it is Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינָּה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion after ruling out רבי in Steps 4–5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה about the נזיר follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.title: What exactly is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view, used in the proof, comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the view of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask for the source of the view it just relied on. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagreeing about when the new נזירות begins. Now the גמרא wants to show us where that disagreement is actually written.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is...?
Prefix meaning 'of' or 'the view of'
Son of רבי...

phrases.english: And what is the view of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the view used in the conclusion of Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The text where רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view about when the new נזירות begins is stated.

steps.title: The ברייתא: does the new נזירות begin on the day of the offerings or the day of shaving?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'וקדש את ראשו ביום ההוא' two ways. רבי says it means the day of the offerings (eighth). רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says it means the day of shaving (seventh).
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a ברייתא: 'And he shall sanctify his head on that day' means the day he brings his offerings. These are the words of רבי. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: it means the day of his shaving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא where the two תנאים argue about which day the פסוק means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the נזיר 'sanctifies his head on that day'. רבי reads 'that day' as the offering day, the eighth. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה reads it as the shaving day, the seventh. This is the exact disagreement that the proof in Steps 3–6 was built on.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall sanctify his head; the restart of his נזירות
On that day
The bringing of his offerings (the eighth day)
His shaving (the seventh day)

steps.whyThisMatters: This one argument over the phrase 'that day' decides whether impurity on the seventh day counts as a new impurity. That is the key point in identifying who wrote the משנה.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
'And he shall sanctify his head on that day' –
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:11

phrases.english: on the day of bringing his offerings,
these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
on the day of his shaving.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא וְקִדַּשׁ אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7 by quoting the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי: the new נזירות begins on the offering day (eighth). רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: it begins on the shaving day (seventh).

steps.title: New משנה: a husband who warns his wife about many men, and a מצורע with many afflictions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list of cases where one offering covers many events: a husband who warned his wife about several men, and a מצורע who was afflicted several times.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who warns his wife about many men, and a מצורע who was afflicted with many afflictions,
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה section begins and adds more cases to the list where only one offering is brought. The next step finishes this line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both new cases have many events: suspicion with several men, or several bouts of צרעת. Even so, as the list's heading teaches, he brings only one offering. The ruling itself is completed in the text that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
One who warns his wife not to be alone with a certain man (קינוי)
A person afflicted with צרעת
Afflictions or marks of צרעת

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It continues the משנה's list of cases where one offering covers many events, which began earlier with the שפחה חרופה and the נזיר.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who warns his wife
regarding many men
and a leper who was afflicted with many afflictions,

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְקַנֵּא לְאִשְׁתּוֹ עַל יְדֵי אֲנָשִׁים הַרְבֵּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the גמרא's discussion of the נזיר back to the משנה, which continues its list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband who warned his wife about many men, and a מצורע with many afflictions, are among the cases where one offering covers many events.

steps.title: The משנה's case of birds brought before a new affliction
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a מצורע brought his purification birds and then got צרעת again, those birds do not count for him until he brings his חטאת. רבי יהודה says: until he brings his אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a מצורע brought his birds and then got צרעת again, the birds do not count for him. This holds until he brings his חטאת. רבי יהודה says: until he brings his אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a detail about the repeated מצורע it just mentioned. A מצורע brought his birds, but before finishing his purification he got צרעת again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, the birds he already brought do not count, so it seems he must bring new birds after he heals again. The תנא קמא ties this to the חטאת and רבי יהודה ties it to the אשם. The גמרא will soon question this plain reading (steps 16–17).

keyTerms.meaning: The two birds a מצורע brings on the first day of his purification
Was afflicted again with צרעת
They do not count for him (do not fulfill his obligation)
Sin offering, one of the מצורע's eighth-day offerings
Guilt offering, also brought by the מצורע on the eighth day

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the birds (first day of purification) with the animal offerings (eighth day). The birds are a separate, earlier stage.

phrases.english: If he brought the birds and was afflicted again
phrases.notes: These are the two birds from the start of a מצורע's purification, ויקרא 14:4-7.

phrases.english: they do not count for him
until he brings his sin offering.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
until he brings his guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of cases where one offering covers many events (Step 9).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Birds brought before a new affliction do not count for him until he brings his חטאת (תנא קמא) or his אשם (רבי יהודה).

steps.title: Asking for the source of the husband's case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking where we learn that one מנחת קנאות covers several warnings.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the source of the משנה's ruling about a husband who warned his wife about several men. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said one offering covers warnings about many men. The גמרא wants a פסוק that teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this? (a request for a source)
The meal offering of jealousy brought for a סוטה

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where do we derive this?
phrases.notes: He's asking about the husband who warned his wife about several men, from Step 9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to the סוטה case from the משנה and asks for its scriptural source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that one מנחת קנאות covers warnings about several men.

steps.title: One law for many jealousies
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'זאת תורת הקנאות' uses the plural 'jealousies' and the singular 'law.' So one offering covers many warnings.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'This is the law of jealousies.' This means one law for many jealousies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. 'Law' is singular but 'jealousies' is plural, so one offering covers many warnings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תורה' here means the one procedure or offering. Because the פסוק pairs it with a plural, it teaches that several קנויים still need only one מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: The law of jealousies (the סוטה procedure)
Warnings a husband gives his wife about a specific man
One law, meaning one procedure or offering

phrases.english: As it is written: 'This is the law of jealousies'
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:29

phrases.english: one law for many jealousies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural 'הקנאות' paired with the singular 'תורה' teaches one offering for many warnings.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the leper's case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a מצורע afflicted many times and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A מצורע who was afflicted with many afflictions,' and so on. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, the repeated מצורע. It asks where we learn that one set of offerings is enough for him. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the husband's case. The גמרא quotes the line, then asks 'מנלן' to find the פסוק behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: Afflictions (outbreaks) of צרעת
'Etc.': the rest of the quoted line is assumed

phrases.english: A leper who was afflicted with many afflictions, etc.
From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה, using the same question pattern as Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that one set of offerings covers many bouts of צרעת.

steps.title: One law for many lepers
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'זאת תורת המצורע' teaches one law, meaning one set of offerings, for many 'lepers,' that is, many afflictions of the same person.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'This shall be the law of the leper.' This means one law for many lepers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a parallel פסוק. The words 'תורת המצורע' teach that one purification process covers several afflictions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Many lepers' here does not mean different people. It means the same person who was a מצורע several times over. The single 'תורה' covers all those bouts with one set of offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: The law of the leper (his purification process)
Lepers; here, repeated bouts of צרעת in one person

steps.confusionAlert: 'Many lepers' does not mean many people sharing one offering. It means one person who had צרעת several times.
steps.whatToRemember: Both cases come from a 'זאת תורת' פסוק, read as 'one law (one offering) for many': many warnings for a סוטה, many afflictions for a מצורע.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'This shall be the law of the leper'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:2

phrases.english: one law for many lepers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13, in parallel to Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'זאת תורת המצורע' teaches one law, one set of offerings, for many afflictions.

steps.title: Quoting the birds case to begin discussing it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again the משנה's ruling about a מצורע who brought birds and then was afflicted, to start analyzing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he brought the birds and was afflicted again, they do not count for him until he brings his חטאת. רבי יהודה says: until he brings his אשם.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the משנה's line about the birds word for word. This is a setup step: the גמרא is getting ready to discuss this ruling next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At face value, the line says the earlier birds are wasted and new birds are needed, with the חטאת (or the אשם for רבי יהודה) as the deciding point. Quoting it again signals that the גמרא will now look closely at what it means, and the next step challenges this plain reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Until he brings: marks the cutoff point of the rule
The purification process of a מצורע (birds first, animal offerings on the eighth day)
The eighth day, when the מצורע brings his animal offerings

phrases.english: If he brought the birds and was afflicted again
they do not count for him
until he brings his sin offering.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
until he brings his guilt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵבִיא צִיפֳּרִין וְנִתְנַגֵּעַ – לֹא עָלוּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After giving sources for the first two cases, the גמרא turns to the third case of the משנה (Step 10) by quoting it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Birds brought before a new affliction do not count. The cutoff is the חטאת (תנא קמא) or the אשם (רבי יהודה).

steps.title: But the משנה said only one offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that reading the משנה as requiring more offerings goes against the משנה's own rule that a מצורע brings only one offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you say that he brings only one offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how it just read the משנה about a מצורע who brought birds and was afflicted again. That reading seemed to require extra offerings, but the משנה already said he brings only one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line 'they do not count for him until he brings his חטאת' sounded like the birds don't count and he must start over. That clashes with the משנה's rule that many afflictions need only one set of offerings. So the משנה seems to contradict itself.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't you say? Used to point out a contradiction with something already said
One offering, here meaning one full set of offerings
He brings an offering

phrases.english: But didn't you say:
he brings only one offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמְרַתְּ: אֵין מֵבִיא אֶלָּא קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the משנה line quoted in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that a מצורע who brought birds and was afflicted again needs another set of offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same משנה rules that many afflictions need only one set of offerings, so the משנה would contradict itself

steps.title: Words are missing: one offering, and the poor or rich status is fixed later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה is missing words. He brings only one set of offerings, and the line about the חטאת is about when his poor or rich status is fixed. רבי יהודה says it is fixed by the אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Words are missing from the משנה, and this is what it teaches: if he brought the birds and was afflicted again, he brings only one offering. But his status as poor or rich is not fixed until he brings the חטאת. רבי יהודה says: until he brings his אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by filling in missing words in the משנה. The 'until he brings' line is not about needing new offerings. It tells us when his status as poor or rich is decided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rich מצורע brings animal offerings, and a poor one brings cheaper ones. The question is which moment decides which kind he brings. The first view says the moment of the חטאת, and רבי יהודה says the moment of the אשם. This removes the contradiction, because he still brings only one set.

keyTerms.meaning: Words are missing from the text, and this is what it teaches
To fix or settle a status
Being poor or being rich, which decides which kind of offerings he brings
Sin offering
Guilt offering

steps.confusionAlert: 'Until he brings his חטאת' does NOT mean the birds fail to count and he needs another set. After the fix, it only decides whether he brings a poor man's or a rich man's offerings.

phrases.english: It is missing words
and this is what it teaches:
if he brought the birds and was then afflicted again,
he brings only one offering.
But as for fixing his status as poor or rich,
it is not fixed until he brings the sin offering.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיָּבִיא אֲשָׁמוֹ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: until he brings his guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 by filling in the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Missing words in the text (חסורי מחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say the birds don't count and he needs another set of offerings
steps.terutzMaskana: He brings one set of offerings. The 'until' line only decides when his poor or rich status is fixed: at the חטאת, or at the אשם according to רבי יהודה

steps.title: The same dispute appears in נגעים, with a third view
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in נגעים has רבי שמעון saying the poor or rich status follows the חטאת and רבי יהודה saying it follows the אשם. A ברייתא adds רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who says it follows the birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: a מצורע who brought his אשם and then became rich, everything follows the חטאת. These are the words of רבי שמעון. רבי יהודה says: everything follows the אשם. A ברייתא teaches that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: everything follows the birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from מסכת נגעים showing the exact dispute it just put into our משנה. It then adds a ברייתא with a third opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a poor מצורע who brought his אשם and then became rich. רבי שמעון says his status at the חטאת decides, and רבי יהודה says his status at the אשם decides. This supports the fixed reading from step 17. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds that an even earlier moment, the birds, decides.

keyTerms.meaning: A person afflicted with צרעת
He became rich
Everything follows, meaning it is all decided by that moment
The two birds, the first step in the מצורע's purification

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת נגעים.

phrases.english: A leper who brought his guilt offering and then became rich,
everything follows the sin offering,
these are the words of Rabbi Shimon.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
everything follows the guilt offering.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן, יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
everything follows the birds.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: מְצוֹרָע שֶׁהֵבִיא אֲשָׁמוֹ וְהֶעֱשִׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the fixed reading of step 17 with a parallel dispute
steps.raayaObject: That the 'until' line in our משנה is about fixing poor or rich status, disputed between the חטאת and the אשם
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in נגעים (רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה), plus a ברייתא with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב

steps.title: All three opinions come from one פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב says all three sages read the same פסוק, 'whose means do not suffice בטהרתו,' and disagree about which offering 'his purification' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: all three read the same פסוק, 'whose hand cannot reach בטהרתו.' רבי שמעון holds it means the thing that atones for him. רבי יהודה holds it means the thing that makes him fit. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says it means the thing that brings about his purity. And what is that? The birds.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains the source of the three-way dispute. All of them read one פסוק, but each understands the word 'his purification' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the poor offering is for one who cannot afford it 'at his purification,' so the key moment is his 'purification.' רבי שמעון says that is the offering that atones, which is the חטאת. רבי יהודה says it is the offering that makes him fit, which is the אשם. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says it is what first makes him pure, which is the birds.

keyTerms.meaning: They all read the same פסוק
His means are not enough, meaning he is poor
His purification
The thing that atones for him
The thing that makes him fit
The thing that brings about his purity

steps.whatToRemember: Poor or rich status is fixed at the moment of 'his purification.' רבי שמעון says that is the חטאת, רבי יהודה says the אשם, and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the birds. All three come from the same פסוק.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
All three of them interpreted the same verse:
"whose means do not suffice for his purification,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:32

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon holds: the thing that atones for him,
phrases.notes: That's the חטאת, which fits his view that it all follows the חטאת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds: the thing that makes him fit,
phrases.notes: That's the אשם, which fits his view that it all follows the אשם.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
the thing that brings about his purity,
And what is that? The birds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source of the three opinions quoted in step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All three opinions come from the פסוק 'בטהרתו.' Each sage defines 'his purification' as a different offering: the חטאת, the אשם, or the birds.

steps.title: New משנה: a woman with several births and miscarriages
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins the case of a woman who gave birth and then miscarried a female within eighty days, and then again within eighty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A woman who gave birth to many children, and miscarried a female within eighty days, and then again miscarried a female within eighty days.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts with the last case of one offering covering several obligations: a woman with several births. Steps 21–22 finish this משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After giving birth to a girl, a woman has an eighty-day period before she brings her offering. Here she miscarries a female within those eighty days, and again within the next eighty. The משנה is building toward whether one offering covers all of these births.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A woman who has given birth
She miscarried
Within eighty days
A female

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A woman who gave birth to many offspring,
and she miscarried a female within eighty days,
phrases.notes: Eighty days is the period after giving birth to a girl, before she brings her offering.

phrases.english: and then she again miscarried a female within eighty days,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the מצורע discussion and opens a new משנה about a woman with several births
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of a woman who miscarried a female within eighty days, twice. The ruling comes in the continuation of the משנה.

steps.title: The last case: a woman who miscarries twins
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds one more case to its list: a woman who miscarries twins.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also a woman who miscarries twins.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one last case to the list it began in the previous step. In all these cases the first opinion holds that she brings one offering for everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The twins come out at different times, each one before the purification days of the one before it are over. Because the births overlap this way, the first opinion treats them all as one and requires only one offering. This sets up רבי יהודה's dissent in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who miscarries
Twins

phrases.english: And one who miscarries twins,
phrases.notes: This finishes the list from the last step. The first opinion's ruling, one offering for everything, is understood here and not repeated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of overlapping births begun in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman with several births or miscarriages that overlap in their purification days brings one offering.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: count every other birth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says she brings for the first and not the second, then for the third and not the fourth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: she brings an offering for the first and not for the second. She brings for the third and not for the fourth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion. He holds that one offering does not always cover all the births.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second birth happened inside the first birth's purification days, so the first offering covers it. The third birth is counted on its own and needs a new offering. The fourth happened inside the third's purification days, so it is covered by the third.

keyTerms.meaning: She brings (an offering)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה does not mean that odd-numbered births always need an offering. A birth needs its own offering when it is not already covered by an earlier birth's purification days.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
She brings an offering for the first
and does not bring for the second,
She brings for the third
and does not bring for the fourth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion's one-offering ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A birth that falls inside an earlier birth's purification days is covered by that birth's offering; a birth after those days needs a new offering.

steps.title: Where do we learn one offering for many births?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that one offering covers several births.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's rule that one offering covers several births. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the first opinion in the משנה. You might expect every birth to need its own offering, so the גמרא wants a פסוק that shows otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it? (a request for the source)

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that one offering covers several births.

steps.title: The פסוק 'זאת תורת היולדת' teaches one offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'זאת תורת היולדת לזכר ולנקבה' that she brings one offering for many babies.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רב ששת: 'This is the law of the woman who gives birth, to a male or a female.' This teaches that she brings one offering for many babies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that a תנא recited before רב ששת. The ברייתא reads the פסוק as covering many births with one offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of one 'תורה', one set of laws, for a male and a female together. So even when she gives birth to both, one offering is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The law of the woman who gives birth
Babies, offspring
This teaches

phrases.english: As a tanna taught before Rav Sheshet:
"This is the law of the woman who gives birth
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:7

phrases.english: to a male or a female" –
this teaches that she brings one offering
for many babies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנלן question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'זאת תורת היולדת לזכר ולנקבה' teaches one offering for many births.

steps.title: 'זאת' excludes combining birth with זיבה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: you might think one offering also covers a birth and a זיבה, so the word 'זאת' limits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think one offering covers even a birth and a זיבה. So the פסוק says 'This.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא limits its own rule. One offering covers many births, but it does not cover a birth together with a זיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'זאת', 'this', limits the rule to births alone. A זיבה is a separate kind of impurity with its own offering, so it is not joined to the birth offering.

keyTerms.meaning: An irregular flow of blood that makes a woman a זבה and requires its own offering
One might think (introduces a mistaken idea)
The פסוק says (to teach otherwise)

steps.whatToRemember: As first worded, the ברייתא uses 'זאת' to exclude a birth together with a זיבה. Steps 26–27 question this and reword it: 'זאת' really excludes a birth before the purification days end together with a birth after they end.

phrases.english: One might think that even for a birth
and for a ziva she brings one offering?
phrases.notes: A זיבה is a separate flow of blood outside her normal times, and it has its own offering.

phrases.english: The verse says: "This."

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אַף עַל הַלֵּידָה וְעַל הַזִּיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule just derived.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A birth and a זיבה cannot share one offering.

steps.title: Why would anyone think birth and זיבה share an offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's 'you might think': by that logic, eating blood and giving birth would also share one offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says: you might think that for a birth and a זיבה she brings only one offering. But if so, if she ate blood and gave birth, would she also bring only one offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the starting idea of the ברייתא. It asks why anyone would ever have thought two different obligations could share one offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating blood by mistake and giving birth are two unrelated obligations, and obviously each needs its own offering. The זיבה offering and the birth offering are also two separate obligations. So the 'יכול' seems pointless, and the word 'זאת' seems unneeded to exclude it.

keyTerms.meaning: But if that were so (introduces a strange result)
She ate blood (by mistake, which requires a חטאת)

phrases.english: It teaches:
One might think that for a birth and for a ziva
she brings only one offering.
But if so,
if she ate blood and gave birth,
would it also be that she brings
only one offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the starting idea that the ברייתא rejected.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's 'יכול' that birth and זיבה might share one offering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two unrelated obligations never share one offering, as with eating blood and giving birth. So there was never any reason to think so, and no need for 'זאת' to exclude it.

steps.title: Rewording the ברייתא: births before and after the purification days end
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the ברייתא's 'you might think' to: one offering for a birth before the purification days end and a birth after they end. 'זאת' rules that out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it like this: One might think a single offering covers a birth before her days are complete and a birth after they are complete. The verse says 'This' to teach otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 26 by rereading what the ברייתא really meant to exclude with the word 'זאת'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 asked why anyone would think a birth and a זיבה share one offering. They are two separate obligations, just like eating blood and giving birth. So the גמרא says the ברייתא's real worry was two births: one before the purification days of the earlier birth were complete, and one after. 'זאת' teaches that the later birth needs its own offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Say it this way; the גמרא is rewording a teaching
You might think (the ברייתא's 'I might have said')
The completion of the purification days
The verse comes to teach

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the limit on 'one offering for many births': it only works while the births fall within the same purification period.

phrases.english: Say it like this:
One might think: for a birth before the completion
phrases.notes: 'Completion' means the end of the purification days from her earlier birth.

phrases.english: and for a birth after the completion, one offering?
The verse says: "This."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 26 by rewording the ברייתא's hypothetical.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say one might think a birth and a זיבה share one offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא really says one might think a birth before the purification days end and a birth after they end share one offering. 'זאת' excludes that.

steps.title: Which fetus sets the eighty-day count
steps.stepSummary: Back on the משנה about repeated miscarriages: for רבי יהודה the first fetus causes the obligation and the count starts from it. For חכמים it is the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'She miscarried within eighty days, etc.' When you look into it, you find that for רבי יהודה the first fetus is the cause, and she counts from the first fetus. For חכמים the second fetus is the cause, and she counts from the second fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a woman who miscarried within eighty days of an earlier miscarriage. It then explains what the argument between רבי יהודה and חכמים really comes down to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the eighty days always run from the first fetus. So a third miscarriage that falls after those days needs a new offering. For חכמים, each new fetus starts a new count. Since each miscarriage falls within the days of the one before it, one offering covers all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the rest of the משנה is understood
When you analyze it, you will find
A fetus or newborn
Causes; here, sets the obligation and the count
She counts the days

steps.whyThisMatters: This boils the whole argument down to one question: does the count start from the first birth or the latest one?

phrases.english: She miscarried within eighty days, etc.
When you look into it, you will find
according to Rabbi Yehuda,
the first fetus is the cause,
and she counts from the first fetus.
According to the Rabbis,
the second fetus is the cause,
and she counts from the second fetus.

steps.triggerLanguage: הפילה בתוך שמונים כו׳ כשתמצי לומר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the ברייתא's source back to the משנה's argument (step 22).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי יהודה the count runs from the first fetus. For חכמים it runs from the second fetus.

steps.title: Why say it? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this explanation was needed, since the משנה already shows it clearly.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'When you look into it, you will find'? That is obvious; that is plainly how it is!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation in step 28 as saying nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה itself already shows that רבי יהודה counts from the first miscarriage and חכמים count from the latest one. So why present it as something you only 'find' after looking into it?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why say it?
That is simply how it is

phrases.english: "When you look into it, you will find"?
It is obvious; that is plainly how it is!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 28 as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A statement that only repeats what is already plain in the משנה has no reason to be said.

steps.title: The point is twins
steps.stepSummary: The explanation was needed for twins. One might think רבי יהודה agrees there that the second fetus sets the count. It teaches that he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed for a woman who miscarries twins. You might have thought that with twins, רבי יהודה agrees with רבנן. So it teaches us that he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the statement teaches something new about twins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twins come from the same pregnancy, so one might treat them as one event and count from the second. The statement tells us that even then, רבי יהודה counts from the first fetus.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who miscarries twins
It might enter your mind to say
Agrees
It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה always counts from the first fetus, even with twins. חכמים count from the second.
steps.confusionAlert: The twins case is in the משנה (step 21, 'והמפלת תאומים'). What the משנה does not spell out is that רבי יהודה's 'count from the first fetus' applies to twins too. That is the new point the גמרא draws from 'כשתמצי לומר'.

phrases.english: It was needed for a woman who miscarries twins.
It might enter your mind to say
that with a woman who miscarries twins
Rabbi Yehuda agrees with the Rabbis,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With twins, רבי יהודה might agree to count from the second fetus.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with twins, רבי יהודה counts from the first fetus.

steps.title: A new question is opened
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a new question that the חכמים were unsure about.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked of them:
steps.whatsHappening: This is only an opening line. The גמרא is setting up a new question, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'איבעיא להו' marks a real question the חכמים were unsure about, not an attack on anything said before. The question itself has not been stated yet.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them; an open question

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the twins discussion ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Not yet stated; the question follows in the next lines.
